concerns.text: User Story 2 (US-2) has no associated Success Criteria. All other stories are linked to at least one SC (e.g., SC-001, SC-002, SC-003), but US-2 lacks a corresponding SC entry, leaving its validation undefined.

FR-005 states the connectivity strength metric is computed by “averaging the absolute correlation values across all ROI pairs, preserving sign.” Taking the absolute value removes sign, so “preserving sign” is contradictory.

Error code **101897695** is used for two different failure modes: (a) missing Inclusion/Exclusion markers (US‑1 scenario 3) and (b) insufficient number of valid subjects after QC (FR‑009 / Edge Cases). Re‑using the same code creates ambiguity and violates internal consistency.

FR-005 wording is contradictory: “averaging the absolute correlation values across all ROI pairs, preserving sign.” Averaging absolute values removes sign, so “preserving sign” cannot hold. Clarify whether the metric should be the mean of raw correlations (preserving sign) or the mean of absolute correlations (ignoring sign).

SC-002 requires re‑running the permutation test with different random seeds to assess p‑value stability, but no functional requirement specifies that the permutation test implementation must accept a user‑controlled random seed. Add a requirement (e.g., FR-016) that the test module must allow explicit seed specification.

The specification omits generation of ROI‑wise correlation‑matrix heatmaps, which the idea’s methodology sketch explicitly lists as a required visualization (heatmaps of ROI correlation matrices for each condition).

The idea calls for investigation of *dynamic* functional connectivity, yet the spec only computes static Pearson correlations per condition and provides no time‑resolved or sliding‑window analysis to capture connectivity dynamics.

The motion exclusion threshold of mean framewise displacement > 3 mm (FR-002) is unusually high for task‑based fMRI; residual motion can still bias Pearson correlation estimates, potentially confounding the connectivity‑strength metric and invalidating the hypothesis test.

FR-005 states the connectivity strength is computed by "averaging the absolute correlation values across all ROI pairs, preserving sign" – averaging absolute values removes sign, so the phrase "preserving sign" is contradictory.

new_concerns.text: The scenario references error code **101897695** (see FR‑011), but FR‑011 in the spec defines a different requirement (valid time‑series verification). The missing‑markers error is actually defined in FR‑010. Update the cross‑reference to point to FR‑010.

FR‑002 excludes subjects with mean displacement > 0.2 mm, whereas Constitution Principle VI mandates exclusion for displacement > 3 mm. The thresholds conflict and violate the project’s non‑negotiable motion‑artifact rule.

FR‑005 specifies computing connectivity strength by averaging raw Pearson correlations (preserving sign), but Constitution Principle VII requires the metric to be the mean **absolute** correlation coefficient. The definitions are mutually exclusive.

Motion exclusion threshold conflicts with Constitution VI. FR-002 excludes subjects with mean displacement > 0.2 mm, while the constitution mandates exclusion for displacement > 3 mm. This inconsistency makes the QC rule ambiguous and prevents reproducible testing. Align FR-002 with the constitution (e.g., use > 3 mm) or update the constitution accordingly.

SC-006 requires reporting mean and standard deviation of the dynamic connectivity‑strength series per subject, but FR-018 only states that the series is output. Add a functional requirement (or extend FR-018) that the system must compute and record these summary statistics for each subject, enabling verification of SC-006.

FR-002 states the system must exclude any subject with mean displacement > 0.2 mm, but the idea’s methodology sketch requires exclusion of subjects with > 3 mm displacement (see Idea → ‘Quality control: compute framewise displacement; exclude any participant with > 3 mm mean displacement’). This discrepancy changes the motion‑artifact exclusion criterion and may affect sample size and validity.

FR-005 defines the connectivity‑strength metric as the average of Pearson correlation values **preserving sign**, whereas the idea explicitly calls for averaging the **absolute** correlation values across ROI pairs (see Idea → ‘derive a single connectivity strength metric per condition by averaging the absolute correlation values across ROI pairs’). The sign‑preserving approach diverges from the intended metric and could alter the direction of the hypothesized effect.

FR-005 defines connectivity strength as the average of Pearson correlation values preserving sign, whereas Constitution Principle VII requires the metric to be the mean **absolute** correlation coefficient across DMN edges. This inconsistency makes the metric violate a core project principle and could invalidate the intended state‑dependent connectivity quantification.
